security_audit.summary: Most static findings in SKILL.md and reference files are false positives caused by Markdown command examples and genomics terminology. The real risk is the workflow generator, which emits runnable bash scripts with user-provided paths and options interpolated without shell escaping.

remediation.issue: Generated bash scripts embed user-controlled values without shell escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Use shlex.quote or a structured template that safely quotes every inserted path and option before writing the script.

remediation.issue: Generated scripts are presented as directly runnable after chmod.
remediation.suggestion: Add a review step and warnings for unusual characters in file names, output directories, and other shell-visible values.

remediation.issue: Workflow script output can overwrite an existing file selected with the output option.
remediation.suggestion: Warn before overwriting files or add an explicit force option for destructive replacement.

content.value_statement: NGS workflows require careful command selection, normalization, and quality checks. This skill guides deepTools workflows for BAM conversion, QC, comparisons, and visualizations.
actual_capabilities: Select appropriate deepTools commands for ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and related NGS workflows.
Generate workflow templates for ChIP-seq QC, ChIP-seq analysis, RNA-seq coverage, and ATAC-seq analysis.
Explain normalization choices such as RPGC, CPM, RPKM, BPM, and read-count scaling.
Guide BAM, bigWig, and BED file validation before analysis starts.
Help create heatmaps, profile plots, correlation plots, PCA plots, and fingerprint plots.
Provide effective genome size guidance for common reference assemblies.
limitations: It does not verify biological conclusions without reviewing the actual data and plots.
It assumes deepTools and required command-line dependencies are installed separately.
Generated shell workflows need review before execution, especially when file names contain special characters.
It does not replace experiment-specific statistical analysis or replicate quality standards.

use_cases.title: Prepare ChIP-seq QC
use_cases.description: Create a quality control plan with correlation, PCA, coverage, fragment size, and fingerprint checks.

use_cases.title: Build Coverage Tracks
use_cases.description: Choose normalization settings and convert BAM files into browser-ready bigWig coverage tracks.

use_cases.title: Visualize Regulatory Regions
use_cases.description: Design computeMatrix, plotHeatmap, and plotProfile commands for genes, peaks, or custom BED regions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: I have NGS alignment files and want to use deepTools. Ask me the minimum questions needed, then recommend the best workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Convert BAM to bigWig
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a deepTools bamCoverage command for my experiment. Explain the normalization method, genome size, bin size, and duplicate handling choices.

prompt_templates.title: Plan ChIP-seq QC
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a ChIP-seq QC workflow for input and ChIP BAM files. Include correlation, PCA, coverage, fragment size, and fingerprint outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Visualization Parameters
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my intended computeMatrix and plotHeatmap plan for promoter regions. Suggest parameter changes for sorting, clustering, colors, and scaling.

output_examples.input: User asks how to compare two ChIP-seq samples against an input control.
output_examples.output: The response recommends coverage generation, log2 comparison, matrix computation around genes or peaks, and heatmap/profile visualization.

output_examples.input: User asks which normalization method fits RNA-seq coverage tracks.
output_examples.output: The response explains CPM for browser coverage, RPKM for gene-length-aware summaries, and why read extension should be avoided.

output_examples.input: User asks why a deepTools workflow is slow or memory intensive.
output_examples.output: The response suggests region testing, larger bins, more processors, pre-filtered BAM files, and bigWig output where appropriate.

best_practices: Validate BAM indexes, BED format, and genome build compatibility before running deepTools commands.
Run quality control before visualization or comparison workflows to avoid interpreting poor input data.
Review generated shell scripts and quote unusual file paths before executing them.
anti_patterns: Do not compare samples with inconsistent normalization methods.
Do not use read extension for RNA-seq coverage over splice junctions.
Do not run generated workflows blindly on untrusted file names or directories.

faq.question: What data types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports deepTools workflows for BAM, bigWig, and BED files used in common NGS analyses.

faq.question: Can it install deepTools for me?
faq.answer: It can suggest installation commands, but the user must install and manage dependencies in their environment.

faq.question: Does it generate runnable workflow scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. The included generator creates bash workflow templates that should be reviewed before execution.

faq.question: Which experiments are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance covers ChIP-seq, RNA-seq coverage, ATAC-seq, MNase-seq, and similar sequencing workflows.

faq.question: Can it interpret QC plots?
faq.answer: It can explain expected patterns and warning signs, but final interpretation depends on the experiment and raw results.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive data?
faq.answer: The skill does not require network access, but generated commands may process local research files. Review paths and outputs first.
